text:
james: ran into a weird crash copying the Python quickstart into a notebook. Paste:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="rwd-mini", input="hey")
print(resp.output_text)
```
I get `RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop` right away.

anika: notebook kernels have an event loop already. Our public convenience method is calling `asyncio.run` which is unsafe in that context. We should either show an explicit `async with`/`await` pattern in the quickstart or change the wrapper.

james: tried `await client.chat.completions.create(...)` in a cell, but then after a kernel restart there were `Event loop is closed` errors coming from background tasks. Looks like token refresher/background tasks are being started by the sync wrapper and not torn down cleanly.

li: this is two things IMHO: (1) docs misleadingly show sync-style usage in a REPL / notebook, (2) the SDK's sync helpers start an auth refresher and unconditionally use `asyncio.run` which interacts poorly with notebook restart semantics.

anika: small repro: open notebook, run quickstart cell, then restart kernel, run cell again — sometimes you see `Task was destroyed but it is pending` or attempts to schedule on a closed loop. Colab behaves slightly different (harder kernel restarts).

james: stacktrace snippet: `File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/sdk.py", line 88, in create
  return asyncio.run(self._create(...))` so the public method is still wrapped.

li: proposed fixes: 1) docs PR — add "Notebooks & REPL" section showing `async with AsyncClient():` and top-level `await` patterns, note `nest_asyncio` as last-resort; 2) SDK change — make the sync convenience wrapper detect `asyncio.get_running_loop()` and if already running, raise a clear error advising the async usage; avoid spawning background tasks when used from a sync helper that uses `asyncio.run` by lazily starting token refresher attached to the loop we create; 3) add a tiny helper `redwood.notebook.create_client()` that returns an async client wired for notebook use.

anika: +1. Also add a test: run the sample notebook via papermill in CI to catch regressions (not heavy, one cell).

devx-bot: created issue #1832: "Notebook quickstart: AsyncClient / event loop interaction and background task lifecycle" (repro notebook attached).

james: opened a minimal GH PR with docs patch and a proposed error message for the sync wrapper. Will add the papermill job in a follow-up.

qa-bot: note recorded: add integration check covering Colab and Jupyter kernel restart behavior in the test plan.

li: can we also add a short note in the SDK's README about what users should expect when mixing sync and async usage? A couple lines would help reduce helpdesk tickets.

anika: agreed — small change with big DX improvement. Tagging @devex-squad for prioritization.

james: thanks all, I'll iterate on the PR and include a minimal notebook that demonstrates correct `async with` usage and a bad-copy example that we warn about. :thumbsup:
